summary: Implemented bounded file-parallel scheduling for the single-pattern Search text sources. The coordinator bounds workers, dispatched files, per-file result chunks and consumer staging while preserving traversal order, typed chunk writes, predicate-before-slice semantics, cancellation and first-failure propagation.

implementation.scopeBoundary: Only the owning repository's Search production/test assemblies changed, plus this scope's campaign evidence. No sibling repository, public package version, publication state or installation changed.
implementation.scheduler: A bounded work channel dispatches at most MaxInFlightFiles file items. A bounded single-reader/single-writer result channel is created per active file, and the FIFO active queue drains completed work in traversal order.
implementation.resourceBounds: The default uses at most four workers, twice that many in-flight file handles, two buffered result chunks per file and one bounded consumer staging list. Each worker owns its SearchCharBuffer, matcher, spans and sink; no per-match tasks or unbounded producer queue are introduced.
implementation.semanticBoundary: Accepted predicates remain inside worker-local typed sinks. The global SearchSliceWindow is applied only while the coordinator drains files in order, and progress is reported only by that consumer, preserving predicate-before-slice and deterministic output semantics.
implementation.failureAndCancellation: Worker failures are captured before channel completion, linked cancellation stops traversal and blocked channel writers, outstanding work items are completed idempotently, and all workers are joined before the original failure or caller cancellation is rethrown.
implementation.counterSafety: Scope counters now use Interlocked-backed increments and atomic reads because traversal and file processing can run concurrently.
implementation.compatibility: Injected reader factories use the sequential option to preserve caller-owned reader state; the production default reader uses bounded file parallelism. SearchManySource and metadata-only SearchPathsSource retain their existing sequential contracts.

gateResults.evidence: The exact Release suite passed across 21 projects with 1,545 total tests, 1,511 passed, 0 failed and 34 classified skips; the Search suite and coordinator-focused tests also passed.

The separate ownership review approved the bounded scheduler, deterministic ordered drain, typed chunk boundary, failure cleanup and explicit sequential injected-reader compatibility boundary; exact commands, tool versions, hashes and the unique trailer-bearing completion commit are retained.

Focused coordinator tests cover fast producer/slow consumer, cancellation, worker failure and repeated cleanup, while the full Search suite covers source semantics, ordering, slicing, binary policy, context and projection behavior.

Worker-local buffers and sinks, bounded work/result channels, bounded active handles, atomic counters, linked cancellation, idempotent work-item disposal and worker joining enforce resource and isolation safety.

knownLimitations: The bounded coordinator is integrated into the single-pattern matches, lines, files and counts sources. SearchManySource and metadata-only SearchPathsSource remain sequential in this scope.
Injected reader factories remain sequential by design because their caller-owned reader state cannot be assumed thread-safe; production default readers receive the bounded parallel path.
The coordinator preserves deterministic traversal order and applies accepted TAKE in the ordered consumer, so it does not claim early scan termination once the global window is full.
